metadata.note: The Utica, Chenango and Susquehanna Valley Railway -- incorporated Jan 11 1866 to build from Utica to Colliersville and from Cassville to Sherburne, which is why the Richfield Springs line leaves the Chenango Valley route at Richfield Junction near Cassville: in the charter it was the main line, not the branch. Construction ran up the Sauquoit Valley from Utica to Waterville (June 1866 to August 1868), over the divide to Sherburne (Oct 10 1869), then down the Chenango Valley to Norwich (1870) and Greene (1872), with the 21.903-mile Richfield Springs branch opening Nov 25 1872 -- 97.662 miles of road in all. The company operated its own trains only from August 1868 to May 1 1870, when the whole property was leased in perpetuity to the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western, which ran it as the Utica Branch, about 95 miles Binghamton to Utica with roughly 25 stations. Greene was the UC&SV's own southern end; the last eight miles to Chenango Forks were built by the separately chartered Greene Railroad, and DL&W trains then used the Syracuse Branch into Binghamton (see oswego_syracuse.geojson and scranton_railroads.geojson for other Lackawanna lines here). Regular passengers left the Richfield Springs branch Apr 25 1928 and the milk train followed in July 1938; the last passenger train over the main branch ran Apr 29 1950. Freight continued under the Erie Lackawanna from 1960 and the New York, Susquehanna and Western from April 1982; the Bridgewater-Richfield Springs track came up in 1995 and parts of the corridor are now trail.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: Every headway here is an estimate -- no timetable has been consulted for any era, including the early-twentieth-century peak. The 1870 date for reaching Norwich and 1872 for reaching Greene follow the physically necessary south-to-north build order and the secondary accounts; the ICC valuation table appears to transpose them, printing Sherburne-Norwich as Nov 25 1872 (the same date it gives for the Richfield Springs branch) and Norwich-Greene as Dec 19 1870, which would leave Greene isolated for two years. The exact dates within 1868 (Utica-Waterville opening) and 1945 (end of the UC&SV corporate existence) are not established, only the years. Running times and speeds are unsourced throughout. Station lists are partial: 25 stations are documented on the main line and 10 on the branch, but only Utica, New Hartford, Clayville, Cassville, Waterville, Sherburne, Earlville, Norwich, Oxford and Greene, and on the branch Richfield Junction, Bridgewater, West Winfield and Richfield Springs, have been confirmed by name. Geometry stops at Greene: the Greene Railroad's Greene-Chenango Forks extension and the Chenango Forks-Binghamton trackage the Utica trains actually used are not drawn.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Opened Nov 25 1872, 21.903 miles from Richfield Junction near Cassville to Richfield Springs, a fashionable mineral-spring resort on Canadarago Lake -- the resort traffic was the branch's reason for existing. It met the Unadilla Valley Railway at Bridgewater. Regular passenger service was discontinued Apr 25 1928. Frequency estimated/unsourced
